picks.file: Madrid alcazar Antón van der Wyngaerde prep.jpg
picks.what: The Alcázar above the Manzanares, pen drawing (detail of a view of Madrid, Austrian National Library)
picks.why: drawn on the spot; the old royal Alcázar and town walls

picks.file: Atlas Van der Hagen-KW1049B12 004-Aangezicht op- MADRID.jpeg
picks.what: Panorama across the Manzanares with the Segovia Bridge, colored engraving (Van der Hagen Atlas)
picks.why: colored general view; Alcázar and skyline above the river

picks.file: Antonio Joli P. Real Madrid ca.1753.jpg
picks.what: View from the south across the Segovia Bridge, painting
picks.why: general view with the new Royal Palace, bridge and church domes

picks.file: 1806-1820, Voyage pittoresque et historique de l'Espagne, tomo II, Vista de la Florida en Madrid (cropped).jpg
picks.what: The Royal Palace from the Paseo de la Florida, engraving in Alexandre de Laborde’s Voyage pittoresque et historique de l’Espagne
picks.why: Royal Palace clear in the middle distance; 60 years after Joli

picks.what: The Royal Palace from the Plaza de Armas, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color; the palace façade with the guard

picks.file: ETH-BIB-Madrid (Königlicher Palast) aus 300 m Höhe-Mittelmeerflug 1928-LBS MH02-05-0061.jpg
picks.what: The Royal Palace and the old center, aerial photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: palace, Plaza de Oriente and the old town in one frame

picks.file: Madrid cathedral 2020 - view from the dome.jpg
picks.what: View from the dome of Almudena Cathedral toward the Royal Palace, photograph
picks.why: color, high resolution; cathedral towers framing the palace

notes: #1 is binned P0 in candidates.md because of its atlas number; the record dates it to the last quarter of the 17th century, so y is a midpoint. #10 (cropped copy of #9): Laborde’s Voyage appeared in parts 1806–20 and the plate’s exact year is not given; y is a midpoint. #12: the LoC record gives 1890 for this Photoglob print. #3 shows the Château de Madrid near Paris, not Madrid. #8 (1760 vue d’optique) is a loose, mirror-image copy; Joli preferred. #4 (about 1680) is only 1000 px wide; #5 is an animal piece with a distant city.
